new.n: Horse thieves' loot in an Indian mound, mouth of the Boone River (1849 legend)
new.pl: Mouth of the Boone River at the Des Moines confluence (Vegors Cemetery / Lott monument area), Hamilton-Webster line, south of Stratford
new.st: Loot of an 1849 horse-thief gang was said to be buried in an Indian mound at the mouth of the Boone River, where it meets the Des Moines. People had dug for it by 1927; nothing was found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis).
new.t: The mounds are a protected burial and archaeological site, and the Vegors Cemetery is nearby: look only, never dig.

new.n: Johnson traders' whiskey and money cache, east of Livermore (1857 legend)
new.pl: About 1.5 mi east of Livermore, behind a cabin on a later farm; also 'all along Bloody Run', the creek south of town
new.st: In 1857 three Johnson brothers, traders, were all killed; they were said to have buried six hogsheads of whiskey and their money about 1.5 miles east of Livermore, behind a cabin on what became a farm. Gold was also said to lie 'all along Bloody Run', the creek south of town. Never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis).
new.t: Find the cabin site 1.5 mi E of Livermore on an early Humboldt County plat. Private farmland: ask permission.

new.n: Marble family's $1,500 in gold, west shore of Spirit Lake (1857 legend)
new.pl: Marble Beach, the known Marble cabin site on the west shore of Spirit Lake
new.st: The Marble family, victims of the March 1857 Spirit Lake massacre, were said to have buried $1,500 in gold on their west-shore farm. It was never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis, from a letter via the Des Moines Register), which cites Sharp's Spirit Lake Massacre (1902).

new.n: Pest-house cave with kettles, southwest of Bellevue (legend)
new.pl: Stone 'pest house' southwest of Bellevue; the underground room was not placed
new.st: Southwest of Bellevue stood a stone 'pest house'. A farmer plowing nearby broke into an underground room holding kettles; a later party found four skeletons there, and a counterfeiter's ring was dug from the cellar. The 'bandit gold' said to be hidden there was never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis).
new.t: Skeletons were reported: if a burial turns up, stop and report it. Private land: ask permission.

new.n: Sac and Fox payment money, old trail from Andrew toward Brush Creek (legend)
new.pl: Wide area along the old Indian trail between Andrew and Brush Creek; no spot known
new.st: $100,000 of Sac and Fox government payment money was said to be hidden along the old Indian trail from Andrew toward Brush Creek. Never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis).

new.n: Iron kettle of stage or bank money, south of State Center (legend)
new.pl: First grove north of the Skunk River forks, about 1 mi east and 8 mi south of State Center, near Rhodes
new.st: A Civil War-era Newton-Edenville stage mail sack (another version: $40,000-50,000 from a Newton bank robbery) was said to be buried in an iron kettle between two trees in the first grove north of the forks of the Skunk, about 1 mile east and 8 miles south of State Center. Dug for; never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis).
new.t: Look for the old grove on the 1930s aerial. Private land: ask permission.

new.n: Brown gang's money down the City Well, Bellevue (1840)
new.pl: The 'City Well' near Brown's hotel, Bellevue; well site not identified
new.st: After the Bellevue War of 1 April 1840, the money of W. W. Brown's gang was said to have been dropped into the 'City Well' near Brown's hotel. Never found. One secondary source (a 1927 folklore thesis), which cites Bonney (1847), Gue (1903) and Cole (1921).
